gap: No result I could open states that the DYNESS 1536Wh's maker listing gives no cycle count, retention threshold, surge figure or warranty term and prices it at $549.99, while the PECRON E1500LFP at $549 is rated 3,500+ cycles to 80%, 2,200 W continuous and 5 years if registered within 30 days.
standout_why: Provisional: I could not open the cited pages (powerstationranking.com/best-under-500 and the three outletpicks.com URLs), nor runtimewise, outageoutfitter or wattstanding. The fetch tool failed on all of them with a TLS error and curl was not permitted. The only rival I read was willitrunpower.com/guides/best-power-station-under-500/, which already normalises cycle thresholds (Jackery to 70% vs others to 80%) and says boost modes are not surge. It covers nothing above 1,152 Wh and does not mention DYNESS or the PECRON E1500LFP. So the normalisation method is not new; applying it to the two 1,536 Wh units is. If OutletPicks' DYNESS entry already carries a cycle rating and warranty, this drops to 1.
decides: It moves the pick from the DYNESS towards the PECRON E1500LFP, with a caveat on the budget. At the makers' own US stores today the two cost the same ($549.99 vs $549), so neither is under $500 there. The DYNESS only gets under $500 at the $449.99 Amazon price OutletPicks reported, which I could not verify. For the same money the PECRON states 400 W more continuous output, a cycle rating with a threshold, and a 5-year warranty. For a strict $500 cap at a maker store, the BLUETTI AC180 at $499 is the only one that qualifies, but it is 1,152 Wh (25% short of 1,536 Wh) and its 2,700 W figure is Power Lifting, not motor surge.

DYNESS 3,600 W surge: it appears only in an Amazon listing title seen in a search snippet, never on a page I opened.

DYNESS $449.99 Amazon price that OutletPicks reported: amzcheck.py was not permitted to run and Amazon returned 503.

The cited rival pages (powerstationranking.com/best-under-500, outletpicks.com under-500 including ?show=73 and ?show=70) and runtimewise, outageoutfitter, wattstanding and powerstationranking's other two pages: all failed with a TLS error, so what they say about cycles, surge or warranty is unchecked.

Other 1,400–1,600 Wh candidates (Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra, OUKITEL P1500 Plus, VTOMAN, ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro): jackery.com returned 429 and the allpowers.com store search errored, so no price or cycle threshold was read.
Usable AC watt-hours versus rated watt-hours for any of the three: no measured discharge test was opened.
